title: transforming using matrices
author: 66b13dde02450b0e64029946
chapter_outcomes: Multiplication of a matrix by a scalar.
Evaluation of 2 × 2 determinants. Singular and non-singular matrices.
Inverse of 2 × 2 matrices. Use of the relation (AB)−1 = B−1A−1.
Linear transformations of column vectors in two dimensions and their matrix representation.
The transformation represented by AB is the transformation represented by B followed by the transformation represented by A.
Applications of 2 × 2 matrices to represent geometrical transformations.

Identification and use of the matrix representation of single transformations from: reflection in coordinate axes and lines y = ±x, rotation through any angle about (0, 0), stretches parallel to the x-axis and y-axis, and enlargement about centre (0, 0), with scale factor k, (k ≠ 0), where k ∈ ℝ.
Identification and use of the matrix representation of combined transformations.
The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or combination of transformations.
Idea of the determinant as an area scale factor in transformations.
